justification: Yes. The target file [ByteBuddyAndroidPlugin.java](./byte-buddy-gradle-plugin/android-plugin/src/main/java/net/bytebuddy/build/gradle/android/ByteBuddyAndroidPlugin.java) is 740 lines long and mixes many separable responsibilities: plugin entry-point wiring in `apply`, variant lifecycle handling in `VariantAction`, legacy vs modern AGP runtime classpath resolution in `RuntimeClassPathResolver`, transform parameter setup in `ByteBuddyTransformationConfiguration`, several configuration/attribute actions (`VariantConfigurationConfigurationAction`, `AttributeContainerConfigurationAction`, `AttributeMatchingStrategyConfigurationAction`, `ConfigurationConfigurationAction`), dependency compatibility rules, and transformation dispatching for both legacy and APK 7.4+ paths via `TransformationDispatcher` with multiple helper enums. That concentration of distinct concerns in one class indicates insufficient modularization.
